chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Ubayda al-Hadda', who said:

I traveled with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in a section of the carriage from Medina to Mecca. So he descended in one of the roads. When he had fulfilled his need and returned, he said: 'Give me your hand, O Abu Ubayda!' So I handed him my hand, and he pressed it until I felt the pressure/pain in my fingers. Then he said: 'O Abu Ubayda! There is no Muslim who meets his Muslim brother, shakes his hand, and twines his fingers with his fingers, except that their sins fall away from them just as the leaves fall from the tree on an autumn day.'

key_terms.الْيَوْمُ الشَّاتِي: An autumn day, characterized by falling leaves
key_terms.تَنَاثَرَتْ: To scatter or fall away (referring to sins)
key_terms.صَفَحَ: To shake hands or exchange greetings

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of shaking hands between Muslims according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) physically demonstrates the intensity of spiritual connection through a firm handshake, interlacing fingers with Abu Ubayda to signify deep brotherhood. The Imam explains that this specific gesture serves as a means of expiation, causing sins to fall away like leaves from a tree in autumn, highlighting the transformative power of sincere social interaction in Shia tradition. This narration underscores the ritual and spiritual significance of *salam* and physical affection among believers as a mechanism for spiritual purification.
